item.title: Major US Infrastructure Outages Are Coincidence, Not Cyberattack
item.description:
Major US Infrastructure Outages Are Coincidence, Not Cyberattack

A recent series of outages affecting major US infrastructure providers, including Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, an unnamed NSA network, and Apple, has raised suspicions of a coordinated cyberattack or conspiracy. Evidence indicates these incidents are unrelated and not the result of any cyberattack, nor are they caused by AI. The failures are attributed to a series of unfortunate coincidences involving old, incrementally patched systems often maintained by hobbyists without adequate backup systems.

🔍 Overview

It has been a difficult week for computerized infrastructure, with outages spanning critical sectors such as aviation, banking, and government. While the simultaneity of these events might suggest a common cause or conspiracy, the evidence clarifies that the incidents are distinct and unrelated. Notably, the failures are not the result of any cyberattack, coordinated or otherwise, and even more surprisingly, they do not seem to be the result of AI.

⚙️ Key Details

The underlying causes of these failures stem from the nature of the technology itself:

  • Age and Maintenance: Much of the infrastructure is old and has been incrementally patched and upgraded over decades.
  • Volunteer Maintenance: A surprising amount of the system is maintained by hobbyists without any recompense.
  • Lack of Redundancy: There often aren’t good backup systems.
  • Centralization: More of the infrastructure is centralized, meaning individual failures have cascading consequences across many different aspects of life and society.
  • Brittleness: Much of the tech infrastructure just barely works; when it fails, it can fail badly.

💡 Why It Matters

Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, and recoverability are essential parts of reliable technology, but they are costs that do not generate near-term profits. Modern shareholder capitalism, particularly private equity, prioritizes near-term profits, squeezing out apparent inefficiencies and positive intangibles. Market competition, which usually nudges companies to provide better services, is often removed in pursuit of these profits. From a quarterly budget perspective, spending on reliability measures is viewed as an inefficiency or waste. Consequently, costs of failure are often pushed onto society, leading to stranded travelers and inaccessible bank accounts. These economic pressures create brittle systems with single points of failure, making them more susceptible to cyberattacks and random mistakes. Fixing these issues requires regulation with enforcement and meaningful fines, as well as stringent antitrust enforcement.

📊 Affected Entities

Entity Status
Microsoft Experienced outage
FAA Experienced outage
A handful of banks Experienced outage
United Airlines Experienced outage
Unnamed classified NSA network Experienced outage; details likely never public
Apple Experienced outage

#Infrastructure #Cybersecurity #Technology #Business

Source: Recent Outages Have Economic Causes - Schneier on Security

item.title: Eclypsium Report: Most Infrastructure Security Fixes Address Bundled Software Flaws
item.description:
Eclypsium Report: Most Infrastructure Security Fixes Address Bundled Software Flaws

Eclypsium’s November InfraTrust Pulse report indicates that the majority of infrastructure security advisories addressing exploited vulnerabilities over the past month involve flaws in third-party software bundled into products rather than code developed by the vendors themselves.

🔍 Overview

The report tracks 373 new security advisories published by 23 infrastructure vendors between October 15 and November 19, covering 3,880 vulnerabilities. Of these advisories, 98 were rated critical, and 38 contained vulnerabilities listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. However, 33 of those 38 advisories fixed exploited flaws in bundled software components, primarily PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH.

⚙️ Key Details

These vulnerabilities pose additional risks for enterprises because, even after a software developer releases a security fix, organizations must wait for infrastructure vendors to incorporate it into their products. “Your exposure to exploited flaws depends on how quickly each vendor rebuilds its products after an upstream fix ships,” the report reads. As of November 20, PHP2Shell fixes were either partially available or had yet to be released for affected products from Fortinet, Juniper, Lenovo, HPE, Netgear, HP, and Siemens. The November 19 release of another 18 PHP security advisories further complicated patching efforts for infrastructure vendors and their customers.

🚨 Active Exploitations

Threat actors are chaining PHP vulnerabilities with other flaws to gain root access to compromised devices. An example is the two PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) highlighted in last month’s InfraTrust report, which are now being exploited in attacks against Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls. Check Point reported that destructive attacks deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts. Other notable active exploits include:

  • Cisco Expressway: CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability added to CISA’s KEV catalog on November 20. On November 23, CISA flagged this flaw as actively exploited after Russian cybersecurity firm F6 spotted hackers using it to gain root privileges.
  • Palo Alto Networks and Check Point: The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and CVE-2026-123039 in Check Point gateways. Check Point warned that this flaw was being actively exploited to gain root privileges and establish persistence on vulnerable devices since late October.
  • Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator: CVE-2026-114625, a critical vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.9 that was exploited in zero-day attacks.
  • Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD: CVE-2026-76418, affecting devices configured for remote-access VPNs. The flaw was exploited in attacks to crash devices.
  • SonicWall SonicOS: CVE-2026-19868, allowing multifactor authentication bypass on VPNs configured with single sign-on. SonicWall warned that it received reports that the flaw was exploited in zero-day attacks.

💡 Recommendations

Administrators should also prioritize installing Fortinet’s October hardening updates, which addressed numerous vulnerabilities discovered using AI models. As AI makes it easier to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, InfraTrust warns that organizations must take additional steps to protect their devices while waiting for vendors to release security updates. These include:

  • Removing management interfaces from the Internet
  • Segmenting them internally to limit lateral movement
  • Investigating previously exposed devices for backdoors that may remain even after security updates are installed

“Patching is table stakes, but what you do before the patch is available and after the exploit hits will determine whether you survive,” the report concludes.

#Cybersecurity #Infrastructure #SupplyChain #VulnerabilityManagement #PatchManagement

Source: InfraTrust warns of exploited supply chain flaws in network appliances

item.title: Recent cyber incidents not linked to AI
item.description:
Recent cyber incidents not linked to AI

Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA—it’s been a really bad week in cyberspace.

🔍 Overview

  • But, amazing as it might seem, these are not related.
  • As far as we know, they’re not the result of cyberattacks.
  • They’re not even related to AI.

⚙️ Infrastructure Challenges

  • Our computerized infrastructure is vulnerable and fragile.
  • Much of it is old, and has been incrementally patched and upgraded.
  • A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense.
  • And more and more of it is centralized: the same systems affecting many different aspects of our lives and society.
  • In many cases, it just barely works.
  • And when it fails, it tends to fail badly.

💡 Economic Drivers

  • There are a lot of technological reasons why this is true, but they are all downstream of the economic ones.
  • The technologies we rely on are built and maintained within our economic system—and that’s where the core problem lies.
  • Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, recoverability—these are all essential parts of reliable technology, but they are all costs.
  • More importantly, they are inefficient: costs that feel wasteful until something bad happens.
  • Modern shareholder capitalism, and private equity in particular, squeeze all inefficiencies out of a company in pursuit of near‑term profits.
  • Competition, with multiple companies competing to do the same thing, is another inefficiency.
  • Monopolization removes that in pursuit of near‑term profits.

🔧 Risks and Failures

  • The result is brittle systems, single points of failure.
  • They’re more susceptible to cyberattack—both human and AI‑fueled—and more susceptible to random mistakes.
  • The more we allow unregulated capitalism to privatize gains while socializing risks, the more we should expect these sorts of failures.

🔄 The Path Forward

  • Fixing this is technical, but it’s political first.
  • It requires changing incentives, and that involves regulation and control.

#Cybersecurity #AI #Infrastructure #Capitalism #Regulation

Source: We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For - Schneier on Security

item.title: Authorities Warn More Major Tech Outages Likely as AI-Driven Upgrades Create System Vulnerability
item.description:
Authorities Warn More Major Tech Outages Likely as AI-Driven Upgrades Create System Vulnerability

Recent weeks have seen a cascade of high-profile disruptions—including a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage, and a JPMorgan Chase banking outage—prompting US intelligence and tech leaders to warn that more such events are inevitable.

📢 Official Warnings

Both Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith have stated that the American public should expect continued disruptions.

  • Jay Clayton (CNN): “We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages.”
  • Brad Smith (CBS): “I think we have to be prepared, frankly, for the coming months because this isn’t the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks … The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now.”

🔧 Why Outages Are Increasing

Microsoft President Brad Smith explained that AI is accelerating the discovery of system vulnerabilities.

“AI has made it easier to find flaws, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.”

Recent attacks have targeted government and commercial systems, including the USDA, JP Morgan, and major supermarkets.

🛡️ What Authorities Recommend

Clayton emphasized that the public should be prepared for significant investment in two areas:

  • Upgrading aging infrastructure
  • Expanding cybersecurity measures

🚨 Outlook for the Coming Months

Authorities agree that any major technological shift—especially one involving widespread changes in computing and applications—will inevitably bring instability. Whether caused by AI-assisted cyberattacks or human error during system patching, more outages appear inevitable as the global information infrastructure undergoes rapid modernization.

#cybersecurity #systemoutage #AIrisk #infrastructure

Source: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages

item.title: Cloudflare Builds DNS Testing Tool Using Flamingo Framework
item.description:
Cloudflare Builds DNS Testing Tool Using Flamingo Framework

🔍 Overview

After a DNS service rollout, unit tests passed and dashboards showed green, but production suddenly broke. Some record changes sat unpublished for hours due to a scheduling bug, causing slow hostname resolution and certificate issuance delays. DNS failures are hard to catch because they are slow, spread across the network, and only partially impact where they cause problems.

🧩 How it works

The Cloudflare DNS team extended Flamingo, their end-to-end testing framework, to test DNS the way customers experience it: constantly, from every data center, and against production. Flamingo’s modular design lets teams add support for other networking protocols. Originally built around complex multi-step HTTP testing, its capabilities have increased substantially over the years.

⚙️ Key details

Flamingo is built from the ground up with Cloudflare’s infrastructure in mind:

  • Built a control plane and scheduler that let teams target specific environments, data centers, or percentages of metals
  • Integrates with custom reporting, metrics, and analytics tooling
  • Needs predictable performance and runs well on bare-metal servers in resource-constrained environments
  • Uses a custom domain-specific language (DSL) consisting of a simple setup-request-response format
  • Written in Rust due to its consistent performance characteristics and strong type system
  • The type system enables modularity through strongly-typed enumerations for input and output in the action runner

With just five lines of code, a script can run anywhere on Cloudflare’s edge and scale to thousands of requests per minute. The data from millions of data points is turned into a graph defining how the service is actually performing in the real world.

Component Description
Control plane and scheduler Let teams target specific environments, data centers, or percentages of metals
DSL Uses simple setup-request-response format, only 5 lines of code for scalable testing
Rust Provides consistent performance and strong type system for modularity

💡 Why it matters

Unit testing alone is not enough for complex network pathways with multiple systems. We need to run constant automated testing against real systems and measure outcomes to make informed decisions on service health. Flamingo measures the behavior of production environments to ensure lower-tier code behaves as expected. The DNS measurements now decide whether a release goes ahead or gets rolled back.

#DNS #Testing #Infrastructure #Cloudflare

Source: Probing DNS at Cloudflare

item.title: Constellation Energy Unbothered by Democratic Concerns Over Data Center Development
item.description:
Constellation Energy Unbothered by Democratic Concerns Over Data Center Development

Constellation Energy, America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants, has dismissed market fears that the recent Democratic midterm victories will slow down data center development. CEO Joe Dominguez described the company as “unbothered” by the political shift, arguing that the market overreacted to election results based on fear that Democrats would not let data centers get built.

🔍 Context of the Market Sell-off

Many Democrats who won control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns. This political shift triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks, which extended to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.

Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and faced the risk of early shutdown. However, the data center development boom and its massive demand for electricity have reversed the nuclear industry’s fate. Constellation is now signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers, including:

  • Microsoft: Signed a deal to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania (the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission calls the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history”)
  • Amazon and Google: Constellation signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to their data centers

💡 Bipartisan Support and Economic Impact

Nuclear energy has enjoyed bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because operating a reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions, making it appealing to Big Tech companies balancing aggressive data center development with ambitious climate goals.

Dominguez noted that the market scare was not lost on Democrats, who do not want to be the reason the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development. He pointed out that Virginia and Illinois, both led by Democratic governors prior to the election, have seen a significant amount of data center development.

In Virginia, the most vocal critics of data centers have actually been Republicans. Senator Richard Stuart, a conservative Republican, has aggressively pursued data center regulation. Last month, Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, denied Stuart’s request for a special session to address a concerning new report from the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality regarding the state’s strained groundwater supply amid rampant data center growth.

🏛️ Legislative Action

The Senate is expected to vote on a sweeping bill, co-sponsored by two Democrats, marketed as a way to speed up permitting for new power plants and transmission lines to connect data centers to the grid faster.

  • Provisions: New Mexico Senator Martin Heinrich, one of the bill’s backer, highlighted provisions designed to protect utility customers from rising rates and ensure Big Tech pays a fair share of costs.
  • Critiques: Researchers at Columbia University SIPA’s Center on Global Energy Policy called the bill’s protections “mixed,” noting they do not account for wholesale capacity and energy prices, which is a principal way data center demand can lead to higher household bills. Senate Democrats are divided, with critics arguing the bill fast-tracks projects at the expense of public input and environmental oversight, potentially leading to a massive overbuild of energy projects that Americans will end up paying for.

#NuclearEnergy #DataCenters #AI #Infrastructure #Politics

Source: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers

item.title: Texas AI Data Center Boom Meets New Political and Regulatory Hurdles
item.description:
Texas AI Data Center Boom Meets New Political and Regulatory Hurdles

Texas has become the new epicenter of the AI data‑center build‑out, but recent election results and a governor‑directed permit halt are reshaping the landscape.

🔍 Overview

  • Texas is the fastest‑growing data‑center market in the U.S. and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI build‑outs.
  • Some of the world’s largest AI infrastructure projects are under construction in the state.
  • Until September, Texas was considered the easiest place to build data centers.

🗳️ Political Shift

  • Democrat James Talarico won the U.S. Senate seat against Ken Paxton.
  • Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against incumbent Greg Abbott.
  • Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years.
  • Both Talarico and Hinojosa made data‑center issues central to their campaigns, discussing them constantly on the trail.
  • Voters supported measures to protect ratepayers from electricity‑bill increases caused by data centers and favored broader bans on new data centers.
  • County‑level voting patterns show mixed support: Dallas County and nearby areas voted blue, while Ellis County (a leading permit‑request county) voted red; Cameron County, a data‑center hot spot, shifted blue, whereas Mitchell and Scurry Counties, home to western projects, voted red.

🏗️ Major Projects

Project Planned Capacity (MW) Primary Purpose
Stargate Frontier (Shackelford County) 1,820 General AI infrastructure (comparable to SpaceX’s Colossus 2)
Nexus Hubbard (under construction) 6,400 Intended mostly to serve Anthropic; second‑largest U.S. data center behind Meta’s Hyperion

📉 Industry Reaction

  • At the DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, panelists lamented the September 21 directive from Governor Abbott that halted data‑center permits.
  • Panelists expected the halt to potentially slow existing projects and halt new ones altogether.
  • Banks and lenders are already becoming pickier about financing these projects.
  • Local officials who have some say over development may resist sweeping state restrictions, because no single office decides a project’s fate.

🔮 Outlook

  • The combination of a newly Democratic‑controlled legislature, a governor‑directed permit freeze, and voter concerns about electricity costs creates uncertainty for Texas’ AI data‑center pipeline.
  • Industry participants are watching both state regulatory actions and local political dynamics as they determine the future pace of construction.

#AIDataCenters #TexasPolitics #Infrastructure

Source: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.

item.title: Anthropic transitions to new internal source control system called Antique
item.description:
Anthropic transitions to new internal source control system called Antique

Anthropic has completed a migration from Git to a new internal source control system named Antique, designed to support significantly higher volumes of daily code changes.

⚙️ Key details

  • The migration was completed in five months by a team of seven people.
  • Anthropic transitioned from a system that would have required over 600 PB of Git traffic per day to the new Antique system.
  • The main branch history is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB.

📈 Scale of operations

Metric Data
Code changes merged (May 2026) ~2,500 per day
Code changes merged (September) >30,000 per day
Daily code checkouts for CI ~25 million

🧩 How it works

  • The system is called Scion, which is described as a reinvention of centralized source control similar to Subversion.
  • The development process involves adversarial review to improve code quality.
  • Skilled engineers are employed to steer Claude and prevent over-engineering in response to hypothetical concerns during the review process.

#Anthropic #SoftwareEngineering #SourceControl #Scaling #Infrastructure

Source: Redesigning source control at Anthropic

item.title: Encore expands platform for building production systems with real infrastructure
item.description:
Encore expands platform for building production systems with real infrastructure

Encore released an update that adds new capabilities for building, testing, and deploying production‑grade systems using real infrastructure throughout the development lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

Encore is the infrastructure platform for the intelligence era, where engineers and AI agents build production systems without waiting on infrastructure.

🧩 How It Works

  • Run and validate with real infrastructure locally and in preview environments, then deploy to your own AWS or GCP account.
  • Declare the resources your app needs (databases, Pub/Sub, object storage, caches, cron jobs, secrets) directly in your code, and encore run starts the whole system locally with real Postgres, real Pub/Sub semantics, and distributed tracing.
  • Each declaration becomes a node in Encore’s application graph.
  • Encore runs the migrations and stands up local equivalents on encore run, and provisions the cloud equivalents on deploy.
  • When you push a change that adds or modifies a resource, Encore diffs the application graph against the environment, provisions whatever is missing in your AWS or GCP account, and rolls out the new code against it.
  • Encore separates application semantics from environment-specific configuration.
  • In code, you define what resources your app needs, not how each environment should configure them.
  • That keeps services portable across clouds, regions, accounts, scale profiles, and local development.
  • Encore provisions every resource with sane production defaults, then helps you manage configuration separately from your application code.

⚙️ Key Features

  • Encore platform dashboard: easy to use knobs for all common settings like process allocation, instance sizes, replicas, etc.
  • Your AWS or GCP console: tweak anything directly in your cloud provider console.
  • Encore picks up the changes on the next deploy.
  • IaC: manage config for Encore‑provisioned resources alongside the rest of your infrastructure via the Terraform provider.
  • The same infrastructure model runs locally, in per‑PR preview environments, and in production.
  • Local: encore run starts the whole system locally: real Postgres, real Pub/Sub semantics, type‑safe service‑to‑service calls, plus a local dashboard with distributed tracing.
  • Infrastructure namespaces let multiple branches or agents work in parallel with isolated state.
  • Open a pull request and Encore sets up an ephemeral environment and (optionally) branches databases from a seed environment.
  • This Lets you do end‑to‑end validation against before merging to a shared staging environment.
  • Production: Push to deploy.
  • Encore diffs the application graph against the environment, provisions what is missing in your AWS or GCP account, wires up least‑privilege IAM based on the application’s code paths, and rolls out the new code.

🚀 Availability

The update is available to users who already have Encore set up on AWS or GCP and can be accessed through the standard encore run and deployment commands.

💡 Why It Matters

By letting developers define what resources are needed rather than how each environment configures them, Encore makes services portable across clouds, regions, and accounts while keeping configuration separate from application code. This reduces waiting time for infrastructure, enables safe end‑to‑end validation in preview environments, and enforces least‑privilege permissions automatically.

#Encore #Infrastructure #DevOps #AIAgents

Source: encoredev/encore

item.title: Amazon Urges Support for AI Data Centers Warning of Geopolitical Risks
item.description:
Amazon Urges Support for AI Data Centers Warning of Geopolitical Risks

Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Gorman has published a blog post calling for public support of AI data center projects, warning that blocking them could cause irreparable harm to the US economy and national security. The publication comes as public support for data centers has plummeted, with communities across the United States raising concerns about jobs, environmental impact, power demands, and AI safety.

🔍 Overview

The push from Amazon comes amid rising local backlash and over 100 data center moratoriums currently being considered across the country. AWS CEO Matt Gorman warned that the United States cannot afford to lose the geopolitical race for AI dominance, stating that enacting these moratoriums would write a “losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.” Gorman also argued that some public opposition is fueled by myths, social media, 24/7 news, and reports of foreign nations intentionally seeding misinformation in the US to trick communities into slowing down the build-out.

⚙️ Key details

To address local friction and establish clearer practices, Amazon is codifying several measures under a new “Data Center Commitment.” Additionally, the company has altered how it interacts with local government agencies:

  • Community Investment: Amazon has pledged to invest more than $1 billion to support communities neighboring its data centers.
  • Economic and Utility Safeguards: The commitment includes practices around creating jobs and preventing increases to local energy rates.
  • Elimination of NDAs: Amazon will no longer use nondisclosure agreements with government agencies. This policy change follows a probe by Democratic lawmaker Jamie Raskin into tech companies’ secret deals with local officials.
  • Shift toward Transparency: Commenting on the change, Amazon chief global affairs and legal officer David Zapolsky noted that while the industry has a history of secrecy, “it just didn’t make sense” to continue requiring NDAs when community leaders need to share information with constituents.

#AWS #DataCenters #Infrastructure #Amazon

Source: Amazon writes scary blog warning communities not to block data centers

item.title: NVIDIA Open Sources NodeWright for Kubernetes Host Infrastructure Management
item.description:
NVIDIA Open Sources NodeWright for Kubernetes Host Infrastructure Management

NVIDIA has released NodeWright as an open-source, Kubernetes-native package manager designed to modify and maintain host infrastructure at scale. As part of the NVIDIA DSX OS open-source software layer, NodeWright enables the declarative configuration and safe updating of Kubernetes node operating systems without disrupting workloads.

🔍 Overview

NodeWright is a component of the NVIDIA DSX platform, which treats entire facilities as single systems (AI factories) rather than collections of machines. It is part of the supporting infrastructure capabilities that include:

  • NVIDIA GPU Operator
  • NVIDIA Network Operator
  • Topograph
  • DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs
  • NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine (NVCRE)
  • NVSentinel

🧩 How it works

NodeWright consists of three main components:

Component Description
Operator A Kubernetes controller that watches for custom resources and manages the lifecycle of changes across nodes.
Custom Resources Used to define NodeWright packages; these deploy via tools such as kubectl, Helm, Argo CD, or Flux.
Packages Container images containing binaries, configurations, scripts, and verification scripts to surface failures and stop incorrect rollouts.

When applying changes, NodeWright follows a specific operational flow:

  1. Cordon: Marks the node as unschedulable.
  2. Wait: Allows critical workloads to finish gracefully.
  3. Drain: Evicts remaining pods, honoring PodDisruptionBudgets by default.
  4. Apply and configure: Runs the package to set kernel parameters, install agents, and configure system services.
  5. Interrupt: Restarts a service or reboots the node if required.
  6. Uncordon: Returns the node to the cluster for workloads.

⚙️ Key details

NodeWright manages the full lifecycle of host-level changes, including installation, configuration, upgrade, and uninstallation. Key capabilities include:

  • Infrastructure Operations: Performs tasks that normally require root access without recycling nodes, such as setting sysctl and GRUB parameters, configuring crash dump collection, creating logical volumes, installing security agents, and remediating CVEs.
  • Workload Awareness: Respects Kubernetes primitives including node selectors, taints, tolerations, and PodDisruptionBudgets.
  • State Tracking: Tracks the semantic version and state of every package on every node to distinguish between fresh installations, upgrades, and downgrades.
  • Dependency Management: Uses declared dependencies to determine the correct execution order.

🚀 Availability

NodeWright is available as open source and has run in production at NVIDIA under the name Skyhook.

#NVIDIA #Kubernetes #OpenSource #Infrastructure #CloudNative

Source: Manage Kubernetes Node Fleets with NodeWright | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: New Composable Highly Available Cluster Deployment with Kubernetes 1.36.4
item.description:
New Composable Highly Available Cluster Deployment with Kubernetes 1.36.4

A new composable, highly available cluster has been introduced, supporting a wide range of cloud environments, bare metal deployments, and popular Linux distributions.

🚀 Availability

The system can be deployed on the following platforms:

  • AWS
  • GCE
  • Azure
  • OpenStack
  • vSphere
  • Equinix Metal (bare metal)
  • Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (Experimental)
  • Baremetal

⚙️ Key details

Supported Operating Systems

The cluster supports most popular Linux distributions, though Upstart/SysV init based OS types are not supported. Support includes:

OS Family Supported Versions
Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04
Fedora 39, 40, 41, 42
Debian Bookworm, Trixie
CentOS Stream / RHEL 9, 10
Alma Linux 9, 10
Rocky Linux 9, 10 (experimental in 10)
Oracle Linux 9, 10
openSUSE Leap 16.x/Tumbleweed
Specialized Flatcar Container Linux by Kinvolk, Fedora CoreOS
Experimental Kylin Linux Advanced Server V10, Amazon Linux 2, UOS Linux, openEuler

Technical Stack

The deployment utilizes the following components and versions:

  • Core: kubernetes 1.36.4, etcd 3.6.14
  • Container Runtimes: docker 28.3, containerd 2.3.5, cri-o 1.36.5 (experimental; available only on Fedora, Ubuntu, and CentOS based OS)
  • Networking & Plugins: cni-plugins 1.9.1, calico 3.31.7, cilium 1.20.2, flannel 0.28.9, kube-ovn 1.12.21, kube-router 2.1.1, multus 4.2.2, kube-vip 1.0.3
  • Management & Tools: cert-manager 1.15.3, coredns 1.14.2, argocd 2.14.5, helm 3.18.4, metallb 0.13.9, registry 2.8.1

🧩 How it works

  • Composable Architecture: Users have a choice of the network plugin for instances.
  • Quality Assurance: The system utilizes continuous integration tests.

#Kubernetes #CloudComputing #Linux #Infrastructure

Source: kubernetes-sigs/kubespray

item.title: Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction
item.description:
Survey Finds Majority of Likely Voters Oppose AI Data Center Construction

A survey of 1,503 likely voters conducted in early September reveals that 61 percent of respondents oppose the construction of data centers used to power AI technology, while 14 percent say they strongly support it.

⚙️ Key details

Opposition to AI data centers varies by political affiliation and voter demographic:

  • Donald Trump voters: Split nearly evenly with 49 percent support and 45 percent oppose.
  • Kamala Harris voters: 74 percent lean oppose.
  • Non-voters: 67 percent lean oppose.
  • Age demographics: AI and data centers registered at less than 1 percent for most demographics, except for the 18–29 group, where 3 percent selected this issue over other popular responses such as inflation, foreign policy, and the economy.

Among those who oppose the construction of data centers, 56 percent support limits, while 38 percent prefer a total ban.

💡 Why it matters

Respondents cited several specific reasons for their opposition:

Reason for Opposition Percentage
Environment/water usage 32%
Impact on local communities 21%
General distrust or dislike of AI 18%
Regulation concerns 10%
The economy 9%

Regarding trust in handling the issue, 40 percent of 554 respondents favored Democrats and 42 percent favored Republicans, while 18 percent refused or did not know. This follows previous polling, including a March NBC News poll where AI polled lower than ICE, and a May Gallup poll showing seven in ten Americans opposed local construction of AI data centers.

#AI #DataCenters #PublicOpinion #Infrastructure

Source: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll

item.title: Kier Group integrates AI tools and develops custom agents
item.description:
Kier Group integrates AI tools and develops custom agents

Kier Group plc, a construction and infrastructure services company based in Salford, England, has adopted AI tools and is developing custom AI agents to enhance operations.

🔍 Overview

Kier Group plc, with roughly 11,000 employees, builds schools, prisons, and large-scale water and nuclear energy projects. The company began embracing AI two years ago.

⚙️ Key details

  • About 40 percent of colleagues use Microsoft 365 Copilot.
  • The remaining employees use Teams Premium, which includes advanced AI features for chat and meetings.
  • Copilot is used within Outlook, Excel, Teams, and PowerPoint.
  • Data is securely stored on Microsoft’s Azure cloud platform.

🤖 AI agents in development

Kier is in the early stages of developing AI agents for specific use cases.

AI Agent Purpose
Safety data agent Collects and organizes safety data for analysis to address risk areas and forward-looking actions.
Safety standards agent Trained on Kier safety standards and linked to job site photographs, equipment images, and drone video.
Response time agent Designed to speed up response times while allowing direct human interaction when needed.

🏗️ Additional applications

  • Drones reduce the need for people to work at height or interact with certain environments.
  • AI is being considered for facilities management to predict servicing needs for building parts like pumps or elevators.

item.title: Trump Administration Shifts Policy on AI Data Center Public Disclosure
item.description:
Trump Administration Shifts Policy on AI Data Center Public Disclosure

The Trump administration has directed the Environmental Protection Agency to stop publicizing or seeking public input on the construction of AI data centers. This change in policy aims to prevent residents from raising concerns about or learning about proposed facilities before construction begins and permits are approved.

⚙️ Key Details

  • President Donald J. Trump has characterized data centers as “big, strong, bold, and Money Machines for the State in which they are built.”
  • The administration has encouraged communities to accept these developments, with the President stating, “You can’t fight it, you have to go with it.”
  • Data centers often require hundreds of acres of land and operate continuously, generating constant ambient noise.

💡 Why it matters

Recent polling indicates significant public opposition to the construction of local AI data centers:

Organization Poll Scope Result
Gallup National (March) 71% oppose
Heatmap Pro / Embold Research National 75% oppose
Franklin & Marshall College Pennsylvania voters 79% oppose

#AI #DataCenters #Policy #EPA #Infrastructure

Source: Data centers are great and we should fully embrace them | Opinion
